body.statement: There exist universal constants \(0<c<C<\infty\) such that, uniformly along every admissible degree sequence, \[\Pr_{G_n}\{c r(n,d)\le R_2(G)\le C r(n,d)\}\to1.\] Thus the exact random-regular full-GATE scale is \(R_2(G)\asymp d^2/[n\log(d+2)]\), which strictly sharpens the bracket in Corollary 5.4 of Kandiros, Harshaw, and Savje on the identical minimax experiment.
body.justification: The theorem closes the named degree-dependent minimax interval with universal constants and an attaining observed-data procedure.
body.gap: The closest published result leaves \(d/n\) below and \(d^2/n\) above; neither endpoint determines the logarithmic stable-set frontier.
body.consumer: The deployed global-rollout problem in Karrer and coauthors receives a sharp precision benchmark for diffuse regular networks.

obligation.what_is_open: Establish the upper half \(R_2(G)\le C r(n,d)\) needed to match the proved all-procedure converse.
obligation.obstruction: The lower half is proved in this dispatch, but the upper half depends on the unresolved stable-kernel operator estimate through \(\text{thm:capsule-upper}\).
obligation.attempted: I intersected the random-graph events and checked the minimax comparison.  This closes mechanically once the kernel theorem is available, but no independent route to its logarithmic upper rate follows from the frozen core.
obligation.partial_result: The all-procedure half is proved here: with probability \(1-o(1)\), \(R_2(G)\ge c r(n,d)\).  If the unresolved bound in \(\text{thm:stable-kernel}\) is established, the displayed calculation in the partial result for \(\text{thm:capsule-upper}\), together with the fact that \((\mathsf D_G^{\mathrm{cap}},\widehat\tau_G)\) is one admissible pair in \(\text{def:minimax-risk}\), gives \(R_2(G)\le Cr(n,d)\) on the same event.  Intersecting the two events then yields the stated matched frontier.  No lower-bound issue remains.
